title: Staged Determinism Contract PRD — Unified Chat/Completions/Embeddings/Rerank + Launch Checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: This PRD defines a minimal contractual surface and launch checklist for delivering a staged determinism capability across Redwood's hosted API endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). The goal is not to guarantee absolute determinism for all models, but to provide a predictable, testable behavior profile and fallback policy that product teams can rely on for production features sensitive to output variance (eg. deterministic summaries, deterministic rerank ordering for pipelines, stable embeddings for indexing).

Context: Customers building deterministic-dependent features (document deduplication, vector indexes that must remain stable across reindexes, or ranking pipelines that expect stable ordering) have run into regressions when we change model version, quantization, or kernel paths. This ticket standardizes how the hosted API presents a determinism contract, what guarantees we provide per-lane, and the operational gating for launch.

Out of scope: Full seed-based determinism across every model and hardware combination; guaranteed bit-for-bit parity across hardware. Not covering multimodal or speech endpoints in this deliverable.

Owner and stakeholders: Product owner: Maya Chen. Eng lead: Rohan Shah. QA: Priya Anand. Design/Docs: Ethan Park. Security reviewer: Leila Gomez.

Objectives:
- Define the contract and API flags (e.g., deterministic_mode: "staged") and what they imply for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
- Provide behavioral acceptance criteria and telemetry needed to detect regressions.
- Define rollout plan: canary, graded expansion, and fallback rules.
- Document trade-offs and recommended customer guidance for latency and cost implications.

Success metrics (short-term):
- Deployed API flag and runtime telemetry for deterministic requests.
- New eval harness with deterministic test suites for each endpoint.
- No customer-facing regressions for canary traffic (<0.1% error increase), and quality regression alerts firing when similarity drift > 7% on seeded evaluation prompts.
acceptance_criteria: API: A new optional request field 'deterministic_mode' accepted by chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with documented values ['off','staged']
Behavior: 'staged' returns outputs with bounded variance for the provided eval prompt set; embedding cosine similarity to baseline >= 0.93 for 95% of samples
SLO: p50 latency delta for 'staged' vs baseline <= 30ms; p99 latency increase <= 150ms
Reliability: Error rate for deterministic requests <= 0.5% on canary traffic and not statistically higher than baseline
Rollback: Automated fallback to 'off' (best-effort non-deterministic path) from 'staged' if token error rate increases by >200% or p99 latency breach persists for 10 minutes
Observability: Dashboard with deterministic traffic slice, per-model variant breakdown, quality regression alerts, and token-cost delta
E2E tests: Integration tests covering seed+prompt pairs for chat and rerank ordering checks, embedding stability tests across representative models and quantization profiles
Docs: Public API docs, usage guidance, and example migration guide created and reviewed by DocOps and Solutions Engineering
decisions: Adopt a conservative 'staged' semantics rather than full-seed determinism to allow hardware and kernel op variability
Expose determinism as an explicit opt-in flag; default remains 'off' to avoid surprise changes for existing customers
Rerank will be treated as an ordered-output contract: deterministic_mode will attempt to preserve order across model variants, but fallback policies are permitted
Embeddings stability will be measured via cosine similarity thresholds per-model; acceptable thresholds set per-model family in separate artifact
Quantized model variants will be considered compatible only after passing the deterministic test harness; otherwise runtime will route to a verified variant
tradeoffs: Latency vs determinism: stronger determinism increases kernel constraints and may reduce batching efficiency, raising per-token latency and cost
Coverage vs cost: verifying all model+hardware combinations is expensive; we will certify a small set of canonical model variants first
Complexity: Adding deterministic routing increases routing surface area and operational burden (more rollout matrices to manage)
User experience: Opt-in flag reduces accidental breakage but increases discoverability burden in docs and SDKs
rollout_checklist: Engineering: Implement API flag, runtime routing and fallback; add deterministic traffic tagging in request logs (ENG-1842)
QA: Build deterministic eval harness (chat prompts, embedding pairs, rerank ordering tests) and run against canonical model variants
Security: Complete KMS/data-path review for any additional telemetry captured (ticket SEC-433)
Docs: Publish API docs with migration examples and 'when to use' guidance; update SDKs with flag support
Canary: 1% of internal traffic for 48 hours against canary cluster; run synthetic regression suite every 30 minutes
Gradual rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days contingent on no regression alerts
Monitoring: Create dashboard and alerts; instrument p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost delta, quality regression (similarity drift), error rate
Fallback automation: Implement automated policy to re-route 'staged' requests to 'off' and page on persistent breaches
Launch comms: Customer Advisory with guidance and known limitations; notify Solutions Engineering and Support teams
Post-launch: 14-day intensive monitoring window and weekly QA re-eval for first 8 weeks
observability_metrics: error rate on deterministic requests <= 0.5% and not >200% of baseline
embedding cosine similarity drift <= 7% (on seeded eval set)
rerank ordering change rate <= 5% (measured on canonical dataset)
token-cost delta logged per request slice; alert if average delta > 20% over 1 hour
rollback_triggers: p99 latency delta > 200ms sustained for 10 minutes
error rate for deterministic requests > 1% or >300% of baseline for 5 minutes
quality regression alert fired (similarity drift or rerank ordering drift beyond thresholds)
any security or PII exposure detected in deterministic logging pipeline
testing_plan: Unit tests for API flag validation and SDK surface
Integration tests covering chat seeding, deterministic rerank ordering, and embedding stability across certified model variants
Regression harness run in CI for every model variant change and quantization job
Synthetic traffic generator to exercise canary and measure latencies/cost in pre-prod
Chaos test: throttling and kernel-restart scenarios to validate fallback automation
Customer validation: Beta cohort with 3 customers (Solutions Eng-managed) for real-world verification
notes: PM note 2025-02-20: Initial cross-functional review surfaced that embeddings teams want per-model thresholds; added dependency on ENG-1842 for telemetry tagging
Eng update 2025-02-25: Prototype routing implemented; observed 12% p50 latency regression on one quantized variant — flagged for exclusion unless further kernel optimization
QA update 2025-02-28: Deterministic harness shows embedding drift median 0.04 on model A (good) but 0.12 on quantized-B (fail) — will block canary for quantized-B
Docs note 2025-03-01: Draft migration guide uploaded; examples for JS and Python SDKs included
